clue.text: Insisted on confirmation from studio model

parts.note: said by the model, 'I am' (ready) is a confirmation, contracted to two letters
what the studio model reports having done: sat for the artist in position

explanation.surface: Someone demanded written confirmation from a model who works in a studio.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a model's whole reply, I'M POSED: what they tell the artist once in position and ready.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose something is to force it on others, which is what someone who insists on it does.

clue.text: Long dog with no head

indicators.note: the dog's word loses its first letter, its head in a down entry

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog

explanation.surface: A dachshund-like long dog that has somehow lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the dog, but it is the verb: to long for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To itch for something is to crave it eagerly, a synonym for longing.

clue.text: Who could replace print I tore apart?

definitions.text: Who could replace print I tore apart?

indicators.note: read as re-place: put the letters of the fodder in new places

explanation.surface: Someone has torn up a print, and asks who could make a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replace' works twice: an artist who paints a likeness could replace a torn print, and re-placing the letters of PRINT I TORE APART gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist who paints likenesses could produce a new picture of the sitter to substitute for the ruined print.

clue.text: Boxes with false bottom in short supply

parts.note: to spar is to box, so boxes gives spars

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its last letter, here the last letter of false

explanation.surface: Boxes made with false bottoms, for smuggling, are hard to come by.
explanation.walkthrough: A false bottom suggests a hidden compartment, but here it is just the last letter of 'false', placed at the bottom of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sparse is thinly scattered or scanty, so there is little of it available.

clue.text: Last of troops drank up supplies found here

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, reversed

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily, so drank gives toped

indicators.note: only the final letter of troops is taken

explanation.surface: The last soldier drank up the supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drank up' reads as finishing a drink, but 'up' is the reversal signal in a down entry; S is placed at the end even though the clue mentions it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Depots are storehouses, places where military or other supplies are kept.

clue.text: Flipping Ulster PM's come round too late

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister, so PM's gives Peel's

explanation.surface: An irate remark that the Northern Ireland Prime Minister arrived late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come round' looks like arriving; here it means waking up.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep in is to oversleep, waking after the time one meant to get up.

clue.text: Admitting some hesitation, biased editor's stuck

indicators.note: letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: skew can mean slanted or biased
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A biased editor, with some hesitation, admits he is stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck' looks like being unable to go on; here it means pierced.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewered means pierced through with a spike, as meat on a kebab is stuck.

clue.text: Rick gets into records with unknown disorder

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
a rick is a stack of hay, a pile
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A man called Rick takes up record collecting while living with an undiagnosed illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rick' looks like a man's name; it is a haystack.
explanation.definitionFit: Epilepsy is a neurological condition causing seizures, a medical disorder.

clue.text: Rephrase order to child after playing nurses (not female)?

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: 'put it away!' is what a parent tells a child after playtime
not her, the female pronoun negated

explanation.surface: A command to a child who has been pretending to be a nurse, minus any women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like a noun in the game; it is the verb, holding NOT HER inside PUT IT AWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To put it another way is to say the same thing in other words, which is what rephrasing means.

clue.text: Country folk, answering vagrant, love butting in

indicators.note: pushing in among the others, so it goes inside
vagrant means wandering, so the letters of answering wander into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Rustic people reply to a tramp while love interrupts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country folk' suggests rustics, but it means people of one country.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwegians are the nationals of Norway, the people of that country.

clue.text: See court spies from abroad crossing ancient city

indicators.note: the spies stretch across, around the city

parts.note: the CIA is the US foreign intelligence agency
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Look at a court where foreign spies operate around an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an imperative but it is the Holy See, the papacy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Curia is the administrative body of the Vatican, the papal court of the Holy See.

clue.text: Diviner decree replacing one abbey's number two released

indicators.note: the decree takes the place of the one
the letter for one is let go from the prior

parts.note: a prior ranks next below the abbot
I is the Roman numeral for one
an edict is an official decree

explanation.surface: A fortune teller's ruling takes the place of an abbey's deputy, who is set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one abbey's number two' reads as one person, but the one is the I let out of PRIOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A diviner foretells the future, so is a predictor of what is to come.

clue.text: Ignoring outsiders, Ethel's parents get cracking and tackle a problem

indicators.note: cracking breaks things up, so the letters are rearranged
dropping the first and last letters of Ethel's leaves its middle

explanation.surface: Ethel's parents, leaving others aside, set to work on a difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get cracking' reads as a phrase; 'get' is fodder and 'cracking' the anagram signal on THEL, PARENTS and GET.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp the nettle is an idiom for confronting a difficulty boldly, like seizing a stinging plant firmly.

clue.text: Grasping Republican unwilling, perhaps, to discover a way to go in America

definitions.text: a way to go in America

indicators.note: holding something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: intestate means without a will, a punning sense of unwilling

explanation.surface: A greedy Republican, reluctant perhaps, finds a route through the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwilling' means without a will: dying intestate.
explanation.definitionFit: An interstate is a US highway running between states, a road to travel by.

clue.text: Firmly attach small part of body

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the hard plate at a fingertip or toe

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for fixing something securely and a noun for a fingertip's horny covering.

clue.text: The Spanish decline to enter Hawaii's capital

indicators.note: going into, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: HI is the postal code for Hawaii
el is Spanish for the
sink means decline or fall

explanation.surface: Spanish speakers refuse to go into the capital of Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline to enter' reads as refusing; 'decline' is SINK and 'to enter' the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Obstructed service during journey? You can bet on it

indicators.note: within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a route is the way taken on a journey
in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and is replayed

explanation.surface: A train service blocked partway through a trip: a sure thing to bet on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests trains; in tennis a let is a serve that touches the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino game where players wager on where the ball lands on the wheel.

clue.text: Players supporting game opponents in media show

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece goes underneath

parts.note: in bridge the four players are North, East, West and South, two pairs of opponents
the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: Actors support opponents in a game being shown on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the partnerships North-South and East-West play against each other, so the compass points are the 'game opponents'.
explanation.definitionFit: A newscast is a broadcast of the news on radio or television.

clue.text: One uses tactic to intercept notes from the East

indicators.note: the tactic cuts in between the notes
in an across clue, read from the east means right to left, backwards

parts.note: re and me are notes of the sol-fa scale
a ploy is a tactic

explanation.surface: Someone employs a ploy to intercept musical notes arriving from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' reverses RE ME to EMER, and PLOY goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer is someone who uses the services of workers.

clue.text: Rejected bananas are overpowering

definitions.note: plural verb phrase, as in 'they stun', matching the verb

indicators.note: turned back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, nuts

explanation.surface: Throwing away bananas that have become overwhelmingly ripe.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to knock senseless, overwhelming someone completely.

clue.text: Rests in which Warhol ultimately invested?

definitions.text: Rests in which Warhol ultimately invested?

indicators.note: put inside, as one is invested with robes

parts.note: to ease up is to rest, so rests gives eases

indicators.note: the final letter of Warhol is taken

explanation.surface: Wondering what supports Andy Warhol put his money into.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: easels are rests holding the canvases Warhol put work into; 'invested' looks financial.
explanation.definitionFit: Easels are stands that support a painter's canvas while the artist works.

clue.text: Shrewd hacker no amateur

indicators.note: the amateur letter is taken away

parts.note: a cleaver hacks meat, so it is a hacker

explanation.surface: A sharp computer hacker who is a professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacker' suggests computers; it is a butcher's chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and shrewd are both words for sharp-witted intelligence.

clue.text: Initially somewhat peaky, everyone I included in cast was indecisive

indicators.note: only the first letter of somewhat is used

parts.note: peaky can mean having peaks, as hilly country has

indicators.note: put inside, so these go within the other piece

parts.note: to shed is to cast off, as a snake its skin
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Feeling a bit off-colour, an actor who was cast with everyone else dithered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peaky' looks like pale and unwell, a British sense; here it is having peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To shilly-shally is to dither, unable to make a decision.

clue.text: Charlie boy getting dressed

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy called Charlie putting his clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is an old past participle of clothe, meaning clothed.

clue.text: An angry speech full of ultimately insignificant wind

indicators.note: containing, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a tirade is a long angry speech

indicators.note: the final letter of insignificant

explanation.surface: A rant that is full of pointless hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' suggests empty talk; it is a weather wind.
explanation.definitionFit: An antitrade is a wind blowing above and opposite to the trade winds.

clue.text: Wife captivated by playful love letter

indicators.note: held captive inside the other piece
the letters of love are played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A wife is charmed by a teasing love note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests a love letter; it is an alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A vowel is one of the letters A, E, I, O, U.

clue.text: Determined to broadcast Hemingway, for example

indicators.note: broadcasting is spoken aloud, so the answer sounds like the name

parts.note: Ernest Hemingway was the American novelist

explanation.surface: Resolved to put Hemingway on the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and resolute in intention.

clue.text: Went fast over stream of light, then dispersed

indicators.note: the speeding word stretches over the other, holding it inside

parts.note: sped is the past tense of speed
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Someone raced across a beam of light and then scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprayed means scattered in fine droplets, spread out widely.
